retrieval_method: Arena web-page reader (functions.fetch_page) and public GitHub partial clones; browser-extracted text summarized below. No external data binaries were downloaded by this review.

verified_page_facts: The target is geological faults indicative of geothermal resources; the public fault set is incomplete and may contain inaccuracies.
The initial private-test labels were manually identified by fault experts; the final prize round uses an expanded expert-reviewed label set.
The distance-weighted Tversky definition uses alpha=0.2, beta=0.8 and a triangular kernel with 300 m support (3 pixels at 100 m).
Submission format text specifies one float32 GeoTIFF, EPSG:32611, 100 m, matching bounds, probabilities in [0,1], and null/NaN outside the bounds.
limits: A browser page read is not a submission receipt or an authenticated upload test.
The organizer says known faults are incomplete; a catalogue holdout is a proxy, not the hidden expert-labeled truth.

verified_page_facts: The task is fault mapping; the page discusses geophysical, topographic, remote-sensing and computational fault-mapping approaches.
The cited Mattéo et al. (2021) work concerns deep learning on remote optical images and topographic data, not this competition's geophysical stack directly.
limits: Background citations motivate methods but do not validate any local prediction or expected score.

verified_page_facts: The release covers northern/western Nevada and eastern California and includes aeromagnetic and radiometric products with related lidar coverage.

The two survey areas have different nominal flight-line spacing (200 m in Area 1 and 400 m in Area 2), different tie-line spacing and varying nominal terrain clearance; the page cautions that actual clearance can vary in steep terrain.
The page marks the data release CC0 1.0.
limits: Page accessibility and license metadata were checked; no source binary was downloaded or compared with the owner-mirrored model feature raster.
Survey block/flight differences are a plausible non-fault source of feature discontinuities, not proof that any particular model edge is an acquisition artifact.

verified_page_facts: The page marks the compilation public and CC-BY 4.0.
It lists Quaternary faults, volcanics, geodetic shear/dilation, magnetotelluric conductance, magnetics, gravity, paleogeothermal features, seismicity, wells/springs and related measurements.
The page exposes downloadable resource links, including Quaternary-fault and paleogeothermal archives.
limits: The page states the compilation is provided as-is and places fitness-for-use responsibility on the user.
No GDR archive was downloaded, transformed, license-reviewed beyond the page's stated CC-BY 4.0, or used in this continuation.

verified_page_facts: The 2026 GeMS release compiles 48 state geologic maps at scales from 1:50,000 to 1:1,000,000.
The page notes unreconciled geologic units across state boundaries and that the release represents bedrock maps where both bedrock and surficial maps exist.
The page marks the release CC0 1.0.
limits: The source page confirms a public geologic-map compilation, not the provenance or correctness of the inherited SGMC-derived raster proxy in owner mirrors.
No source database binary was downloaded or validated here.

verified_page_facts: The article models stress and strain at representative structural discontinuities in Great Basin hydrothermal systems.

Its abstract reports prior classifications of 313 known systems and highlights stepovers and fault terminations as common settings; the modeling is process-based support for a structural hypothesis, not a map-wide fault detector.
limits: The paper's hydrothermal-system population is not identical to the competition target population of all hidden fault traces.
No claim is made that a particular local geophysical pattern uniquely diagnoses a fault or geothermal resource.

verified_page_facts: The paper is titled Automatic Fault Mapping in Remote Optical Images and Topographic Data With Deep Learning and is marked open access under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
limits: It supports the general use of image/terrain learning, not the validity of the proposed potential-field interactions or a competition score.

verified_page_facts: The public reference repository describes a U-Net baseline and provides CPU-only and GPU environments; the README says GPU training is faster.
limits: A reference implementation is a baseline, not an official score or independent verification of this checkout's evaluator.
These are public-board observations for other participants, not local HOLDOUT-DTI measurements.
They are not submission-page receipts for any GEMSDOE artifact and must not be labeled ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED under the user's receipt rule.

owner_site_review.scope: Public page review for GEMSDOE66-69 and GEMSDOE71-72, plus a current partial-Git scan of GEMSDOE66-72.
owner_site_review.authority_limit: Owner-authored pages and owner GitHub files are inherited claims, not organizer receipts.

sites.current_page_method: 1 m + 3 m LiDAR scarp products, Steger/Frangi line responses, road/canal filtering and relief-balanced spatial CV.
sites.artifact_binding_caveat: The published LIDAR-05 headline names a 24,000-dot file, while linked run-card content uses run_id/lane names LIDAR-03 and a lidar03_full arm. Do not treat the score as independently bound to the headline artifact without resolving that discrepancy.
sites.uniqueness_scope_claimed_by_page: 60 registry rasters; not the 862-row inherited index or a complete current owner-site inventory.

sites.current_page_method: OVTR map-cover emission using an HGB head and greedy 3-pixel kernel coverage; page also contains separate orientation/tip lanes.
sites.score_policy: The page's OVTR headline omits a verifiable 95% CI/evaluator identity in the retrieved summary; excluded from quantitative comparisons. A separate H67A lane has a complete but much lower HOLDOUT-DTI receipt; it is not substituted for OVTR.
sites.limits: The page explicitly says no organizer score exists for its candidate.

sites.current_page_method: Auto-context stacked refinement with multiscale, multi-physics inputs and nested spatial validation.
sites.comparability_caveat: The public run card lists evaluator implementation hashes that differ from this checkout's pinned implementation, and its fold parameters include a 2-pixel exclusion and 5.2-km core separation. The shared version label alone does not make it an exact replication.
sites.uniqueness_scope_claimed_by_page: 69 rasters; the local current seven-repository inventory is broader but still not the complete family inventory.

sites.current_page_status: The page says DO NOT SUBMIT and offers no TIFF/ZIP; it reports a literal forward-overlap stop against family rasters.
sites.limits: Page summary does not provide a complete evaluator version for its listed holdout, so no DTI value is imported into the ranked comparison.

sites.current_page_method: Hydrothermal-structural conduit/alteration-demagnetization combination with GDR 1391 features.
sites.score_integrity_warning: The page calls the user-reported H33 value 0.2778 ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED; this review rejects that classification because no submission-page receipt was found.

sites.current_page_method: H72-1 directly rasterizes and thins SGMC-derived off-catalogue fault traces; additional listed ideas include raw magnetic-gradient and structural-tip arms.
sites.score_policy: The retrieved H72-1 summary does not expose evaluator version and withheld-positive count; do not use its DTI claim in the comparative ranking.
sites.validation_caveat: A score against an SGMC-derived off-catalogue truth is proxy performance, not hidden organizer truth; using SGMC-derived traces as both candidate source and proxy truth is circular for novelty claims.

historical_claims.h33_reported_value: 0.2778 is a user/page-reported historical leaderboard claim, not a HOLDOUT-DTI result; it lacks an authenticated submission-page receipt and is not ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED.
historical_claims.prompt_leaderboard_values: Conflicting historical values remain user-supplied claims; the public page observation is recorded separately above.
